download.html.title: Mac preview & installation
download.html.intro: A small app for your menu bar. A careful path to your Mac.
download.html.body:
The public Mac download is not open yet.
The current development build still needs distribution signing, Apple notarization and completed compatibility checks. The browser preview is available now.

Mac preview · preparing

Download for Mac

Use the browser preview →

What the Mac app needs

HardwareApple silicon Mac. Intel release not available.
macOSBuild target: macOS 14+. Testing so far used macOS 27.0.1; the minimum supported release is not yet established.
App accessAccessibility permission, only for correcting inside apps you enable.
Optional contextRequires a compatible on-device model on macOS 26 or later. Basic correction does not require AI.
iPhone / iPadBrowser preview only. No native iOS keyboard has been released.

Current status

Version 0.18.0 is an open-source development preview. The Mac app has automated coverage for keyboard recovery, Unicode-safe editing and Undo. It now leaves skipped bulk input alone on later keystrokes. The website has separate Chrome and Safari checks for correction and standard Undo/Redo. Web checks do not establish native Mac compatibility.

Everyday physical typing, real IME switching, fresh installation on another Mac, older macOS versions, VoiceOver and the final signed installer remain release gates. The source is available for developers; the general Mac download stays closed.

View source on GitHub →

Once the verified download is available

  1. Download and unzip idkthen. Move it to Applications, then open it.
  2. Find idkthen in the menu bar. Choose English plus up to three other languages.
  3. Try a correction and Undo in Getting Started before granting app access.
  4. Allow Accessibility in System Settings → Privacy & Security. Reopen idkthen if needed.
  5. Add one app, turn on While You Type, and test in a multiline text field. Start with Suggest if you want to review every change.

If macOS reports an unidentified developer or cannot verify this download, stop and check the release. We do not recommend disabling Gatekeeper or removing quarantine.

Updates that you control

This preview does not install updates automatically. A future verified release will appear on this page with its version and SHA-256 checksum. Quit idkthen before replacing the app, keep it in Applications, and check Accessibility after reopening.

Read release notes · Get setup help

help.html.title: A little help getting started.
help.html.intro: Set up once. Keep the everyday experience small.
help.html.body:
Start in the menu bar

idkthen lives in the menu bar rather than the Dock. Open its menu, choose Languages, then add the apps where you want help. Each app can inherit your default languages or use its own set.

Right-click the menu-bar icon for On/Off, a temporary pause for the current app and Undo. Open at Login is in Settings and becomes available after installation in Applications. These native controls remain under release validation.

If nothing changes

  1. Check that While You Type is on and that the current app is enabled. The home status distinguishes a connected text area, a paused app and an unsupported field; on alone does not mean every field works.
  2. Open Settings and check Accessibility. If the app was replaced, quit and reopen it after refreshing permission in System Settings. macOS may ask you to authenticate directly.
  3. Use a multiline text area. Search bars, single-line text fields, passwords and protected editors are skipped.
  4. Finish a word with Space. Pasting a paragraph does not trigger automatic correction.
  5. Try More → Try Typing. If that works while another app does not, the app’s editable text interface may be unsupported. Use More → Review Text, paste a sample and copy the reviewed result as a fallback. If Apply reports that the app did not confirm the replacement, check the original field before retrying.

When another spell checker changes your words

idkthen cannot safely identify or reverse every correction made by macOS, a browser or another extension. First pause idkthen and try an invented example again. If the same change still happens, check that app’s spelling or writing-assistant settings. In Mac apps that offer it, Edit → Spelling and Grammar → Correct Spelling Automatically controls that app’s correction. Change only the setting you want; idkthen never turns it off for you. The website editor and idkthen’s own practice editor already disable their built-in autocorrection.

Keyboard layouts

Korean recovery uses standard two-set keys against US QWERTY. Three-set, Dvorak, Colemak and custom layouts are not supported. The Mac app pauses layout recovery when the active input source has no supported mapping, while accent review can continue. Switching input sources also cancels a pending correction. A Latin word entered on US QWERTY still assumes two-set Korean as its target; do not enable Korean automatic recovery if you intend a three-set target. The browser cannot detect your system input source.

When a correction is wrong

Open idkthen and use Undo Last Correction within two minutes. Keyboard Shortcuts also offers ⌃ ⇧ Z; actual global shortcut delivery is still under validation. It can preserve later words when the original text and anchors still match. Editing the corrected word or switching fields can invalidate recovery; idkthen will avoid applying a stale undo.

After Undo, Always Keep saves that spelling in one click, even with Learn From Undo off. Words to Keep protects names and terms. With Learn From Undo on, undoing the same word in three separate corrections keeps it across apps. You can forget saved words in Settings → Words to Keep. Its More menu resets learned words and partial counts. Ignoring a suggestion is not permanent training.

What can I try on this website?

Open the language button below the editor to choose up to four languages, including English. It also contains Automatic and Suggest modes. Press Space after typing, or click the Space button for the starting example. Language example buttons demonstrate a correction immediately; they append to your own writing instead of replacing it. Undo and Clear work only inside the demo. Use the Undo correction button: standard browser undo does not reliably restore automatic corrections yet. Watch the guided walkthrough.

LanguageType + SpaceExample result
Spanishmananamañana
Frenchfrancaisfrançais
Koreanchromedptjchrome에서
Portuguese (Brazil)coracaocoração
Germanstrassestraße, after confirmation
Italianpercheperché
Russianghbdtnпривет
Ukrainianghbdsnпривіт, after confirmation

Try Spanish + French with reunion to see two valid readings. English resume stays your choice with French enabled. The browser uses authored recognition and exact keyboard conversion, separately from the Mac dictionary and AI model. Korean recovery also checks up to 96 characters on the current line: common words can apply automatically, while short readings need Korean context and unfamiliar readings wait for a choice. English phrases, protected terms and literal/code examples remain unchanged. Conversational forms such as 가서, 하겠징 and 힘듬 are recognized without changing their style. Selected-language shorthand such as lol, mdr, vc and cmq stays as typed. The lists are small and authored; this is not a live slang database. It does not rewrite grammar or infer every name or new expression.

Automatic correction runs on typed Space. Return leaves the word as typed, matching the Mac app and avoiding a change as you send a message. Commas and terminal punctuation are preserved. Moving the cursor dismisses an old choice; replacing selected text does not trigger automatic correction. Explicit example buttons also run the demo rules. Pasting and IME composition are left alone. Text is limited to 4,000 characters and is not saved by idkthen. Clearing the demo also forgets its temporary keep list.

Report a problem without sharing your writing

In the Mac app, open Settings → Help & About → Save Diagnostic Report. The file includes version, macOS, permission state and setting counts. It leaves out typed text, app names, learned words and account details. Nothing is sent automatically.

For a useful report, add the app name and version, selected languages, what you expected, what happened, and a short invented example that reproduces it. Avoid including real conversations or passwords. Email im.minwookshin@gmail.com. The link opens your email app; you decide what to include and send.

Pause, quit or remove

Pause an enabled app for ten minutes from its settings, or turn off While You Type. To remove idkthen, turn off Open at Login in Help & About, quit from More, remove it from Applications and revoke Accessibility. Forget learned words before uninstalling if you want to remove that memory.

privacy.html.title: Your words stay with you.
privacy.html.intro: Data handling for the current idkthen preview. Updated October 21, 2026.
privacy.html.body:
The browser preview

Text is processed in the current tab. The demo does not send what you type to a server, call an AI service, use analytics or save your text in cookies, local storage or a database. Clear removes the current text and temporary keep list. Leaving the page clears them in the demo; the browser itself may have its own session behavior.

The website host receives ordinary requests needed to serve the site, which may include an IP address and browser information. The site is public and does not require sign-in. The hosting infrastructure may also set security cookies and add bot-protection scripts. Hosting behavior is separate from idkthen’s local text processing. This page describes the application behavior; it does not promise that the hosting provider keeps no logs.

The Mac app

Correction uses local rules and macOS dictionaries. Optional context checking uses an available on-device model. idkthen has no account, advertising SDK or background text upload.

When While You Type is on, Accessibility allows idkthen to read and replace editable text in apps you explicitly enable. The app observes supported fields in the frontmost enabled app. Secure fields and unsupported interfaces are skipped. Turn the feature off to stop this observation.

What is saved locally

Language choices, enabled apps, per-app language profiles, preferences, manually kept words and undo-learning counts are stored in macOS preferences. These may contain terms you chose to keep. Full writing sessions and typed sentences are not persisted by idkthen.

Recent correction state and bounded context are held in memory for correction and recovery. They are not a permanent writing history. On-device services and macOS are subject to Apple’s own system behavior.

Your controls

Turn off Learn From Undo to stop additional learning. Existing saved words remain until you forget them in Settings → Words to Keep → More → Reset Learned Words. Edit the manual keep list separately. Remove an app from Apps to stop observing it. Turn off While You Type or revoke Accessibility to stop cross-app correction.

Diagnostic files

A diagnostic report is created only when you choose Save Diagnostic Report and select a destination. It contains version, system version, architecture, permission state and setting counts. It excludes typed text, learned words, app names, file paths, clipboard content and account identifiers. It is saved locally and is never sent automatically.

Support and privacy questions

Contact im.minwookshin@gmail.com. If you email a report, the recipient and email providers receive the message and any attachments you choose to send. Reports are not uploaded by idkthen. You can ask about or request deletion of a support message through the same address.

This preview

The website is hosted with OpenAI Sites. The browser preview is public; the Mac download is still being prepared. If a future feature changes data handling, this page will be updated before that feature is enabled.

release-notes.html.title: Small changes. Clear records.
release-notes.html.intro: Development release notes. A version here does not mean a public Mac download is available.
release-notes.html.body:
0.18.0 · idkthen, open source

October 26, 2026 · source preview; public Mac installer pending

  • Renamed the app and website to idkthen. The internal Mac identifier stays unchanged to preserve existing settings.
  • Added a guard against correcting previously skipped bulk input on a later keystroke. Accessibility inspection now uses a fixed 20 ms window rather than restarting its delay for every signal.
  • The web preview preserves browser Undo/Redo. Corrections run after the current input transaction and recheck the text and caret before applying.
  • Published the code under MIT with build instructions and checked release tooling.

This is a development preview. A signed and notarized Mac installer, broader runtime testing and everyday-use validation are still pending.

Web update · A guided browser demo

October 23, 2026

Watch the walkthrough: Spanish and French accents, a mixed English–Korean word, and a choice between valid spellings. All four languages stay enabled. Play, pause, skip to a scene or undo a correction, then try your own words. Playback uses the existing browser rules; it is not Mac footage or a latency benchmark.

0.17.1 · A quieter menu-bar app

October 23, 2026 · local candidate, public Mac download closed

  • Remember On/Off across restarts. Missing access stops observation while preserving your chosen setting.
  • Added a native quick menu for On/Off, temporary app pause and Undo. Configured launches no longer automatically open a panel.
  • Moved Open at Login into the first Settings section. A development-folder build cannot register itself for login.

Controlled Chrome checks cover correction, later typing plus button Undo, app pause/resume and protected fields. A fast automation burst was not corrected until later input; physical sustained typing remains to be validated. Menu-bar right-click, login/logout, actual IME and another Mac still need final-build checks.

0.17.0 · Keep your intent

October 22, 2026 · local candidate, public Mac download closed

  • Valid dictionary spellings require an explicit choice, including with only one partner language. A context model cannot override this protection.
  • Home shows the current app’s connection state. Undo offers an optional Always Keep action; saved words survive restart without enabling automatic learning.
  • Input-source changes cancel pending corrections. Unsupported source layouts pause automatic layout recovery; three-set target layouts remain unsupported.
  • The web preview preserves English reunion and intentional German ASCII spellings until you choose a reading. Space triggers correction; Return leaves spelling unchanged.

These protections reduce specific failure paths; they are not a general language-accuracy or everyday-use claim.

0.16.2 · Local browser fixes

October 22, 2026

Controlled Safari and Chrome text areas and rich-text fields passed automatic corrections, button Undo preserving later typing and formatting checks. Protected fields and paste were left alone. This supersedes the browser failures recorded below for 0.16.1. IME, physical sustained typing, global shortcuts and service-specific editors still need independent validation.

0.16.1 · Clearer connection feedback

October 21, 2026 · local candidate, public Mac download closed

  • Added content-free connection feedback in app settings and Getting Started, including unconfirmed replacements. Home stays small.
  • Prepared one-command local verification with build hashes and logs. OS integration checks remain pending until performed on the final signed build.
  • Release packaging now also requires update/removal, sustained typing and global Undo shortcut evidence.

Safari selection import worked, but applying the correction did not change the original test field. Chrome correction is not confirmed. No browser integration fix or public Mac release is claimed.

0.16.0 · Conversation rules on Mac

October 21, 2026 · development preview

  • Ported the authored mixed Korean conversation rules and selected-language chat shorthand protection to the native planner.
  • Aligned native spacing, icon frames and system typography.
  • Controlled TextEdit mixed-language correction and button Undo passed on the exact local build. This does not verify real IME switching or the global Undo shortcut.

The frozen synthetic scenario set passed 127 of 130 cases, with three French/Portuguese accent-recovery misses. This is not a user accuracy estimate.

Web update · First impressions and everyday language

October 21, 2026

  • A quieter first screen with a larger headline, one working typing surface, a Space button and compact language controls.
  • The writing area grows with short conversations. Correction feedback moves independently of your text, and reduced motion is respected.
  • More authored Korean conversational endings, including rktj → 가서, gkrpTwld → 하겠징 and glaema → 힘듬.
  • More examples in the existing eight partner languages, with selected-language chat shorthand protected. Ambiguous accents and Ukrainian readings still wait for a choice.

The Mac app and its closed download status are unchanged. These browser rules do not claim general language understanding.

Web update · Mixed-language typing

October 21, 2026

  • Fixed ordinary Korean words missing from the original sample-only vocabulary. Recover sksms → 나는 and wlrma → 지금 while preserving English between Korean words.
  • Short sj → 너 can apply in recent Korean context. Unfamiliar full-syllable readings require a choice.
  • Preserve punctuation, support Enter as a word boundary and keep existing text when editing in the middle.
  • Dismiss stale choices when moving the cursor, and leave selection replacement and pasted paragraphs alone.

Processing stays in the tab without an AI request. The native Mac app and download status are unchanged.

Web update · A smaller typing demo

October 21, 2026

  • Reduced the home page to one interactive editor. Language choices and correction mode open in a small settings dialog.
  • Examples show real demo corrections in one click while preserving text you entered. Keyboard typing, suggestions and Undo remain available.
  • Capitalized demo words require a choice. Unsupported uppercase Korean sequences stay literal.
  • A future Mac download must match this site and the exact release version. The current Mac download is still closed.

The native Mac build remains 0.15.0.

0.15.0 · Simpler web, safer typing

October 21, 2026 · development preview

  • Rebuilt the website around one typing demo with a white and black design and an original idkthen mark.
  • Preserve repeated Latin chat expressions such as gogo in Korean context. Exact Korean two-set laughter still works.
  • Ask for an explicit choice between the name Sara and the Italian verb sarà, including lowercase typing.
  • Added a reproducible native scenario evaluator. Some French and Portuguese accent recovery still needs review; this is not a general accuracy claim.

The public Mac download remains closed until signing, notarization and external-app checks pass.

0.14.1 · Public web preview

October 21, 2026 · development preview

  • The browser preview is public and works without signing in.
  • Added a support email on the website and in the Mac app’s Help & About.
  • Prepared a checked handoff from a notarized Mac package to this website. The public Mac download remains closed while release checks are pending.

The Mac typing engine and background work are unchanged.

0.14.0 · Distribution preparation

October 21, 2026 · development preview

  • Added a lightweight website with a browser-local typing preview, language choices, ambiguous suggestions and safe Undo.
  • Added Mac Help & About, user-controlled Open at Login through macOS, and a local diagnostic report that excludes writing and personal identifiers.
  • Prepared a Developer ID signing, notarization and verified-download workflow. No public release is claimed until its checks pass.

Correction rules and on-device AI behavior in the Mac engine remain unchanged from 0.13.

0.13.0 · Quieter everyday typing

  • Recent correction Undo can keep words typed afterward when the original text still matches.
  • Added temporary app pauses, quieter repeat suggestions, a first-run typing exercise and supported-field checks.
  • Reduced suggestions for ordinary readings in manual text review.

Known limits

  • The web preview keeps corrections in browser Undo/Redo. The Undo correction button restores just the recent correction while preserving later typing. Browser or extension behavior outside the tested Chrome and Safari versions may differ.
  • The current Mac bundle is a local preview, not a notarized public release.
  • Controlled Safari and Chrome checks passed on 0.16.2; focused Chrome checks passed on 0.17.1 with the fast-input limitation noted above. These checks do not certify every website, physical typing, IME or the final distribution build.
  • The build targets macOS 14+, but only macOS 27.0.1 on Apple silicon has been used for local QA. An older runtime, another Mac and Intel have not been validated.
  • Russian uses standard PC letter positions, not a phonetic layout. Ukrainian automatic correction depends on a reliable system dictionary.
  • Browser results use authored recognition and keyboard conversion; they are not performance or accuracy results for the Mac app. Unfamiliar wording and full grammar correction remain outside automatic recovery.
  • No automatic updater or native iOS keyboard is released.

Current release status →
